title: Enterprise Onboarding & Support Playbook — Comprehensive
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose:
This playbook provides a single, consolidated reference for Redwood Inference Customer Success, Support, and Solutions Engineering teams running enterprise onboarding, integration, operational runbooks, escalation response, and QBR/health checks. It is intended for CSMs, Solutions Engineers, Support Engineers, and on-call SREs.

Scope:
- Enterprise onboarding (self-hosted/private & dedicated)
- Integration validation and reference checks
- Known issues & workarounds catalog
- Support process and SLAs
- Escalation playbook and incident comms
- Quarterly business review (QBR) / health check templates and metrics

Navigation and owner:
- Primary owner: Customer Success (CSM Lead) — Aisha Patel (aisha@redwood.com)
- Secondary owners: Solutions Engineering (Marco Ruiz), Support Escalations (Jordan Lee)

1) Onboarding Phases (high level)

1. Discovery (1-2 weeks)
   - Goals: understand workload, security profile, expected QPS/throughput, privacy/regulatory constraints, model choices, and success criteria.
   - Deliverables: Integration checklist, network & IP allowlist, billing/contract notes, initial eval dataset, performance targets (p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec).

2. Provisioning & Access (1-3 days)
   - Actions:
     1. Create customer org in Redwood Console; assign CSM and SE.
     2. Generate API keys (scoped) and create tech contact list.
     3. If Private deployment: provision VPC peering or VPN and provide KMS/HSM ARN templates.
   - Requirements table:
     | Requirement | Details | Owner | Notes |
     |---|---:|---|---|
     | API endpoints & domains | api.redwood.ai, events.redwood.ai | Redwood Platform | TLS 1.3 required |
     | Network ports | 443 outbound to Redwood IP ranges | Customer NW | See IP ranges below |
     | IP allowlist (example) | 35.200.10.0/24, 34.120.5.0/24 | Customer NW / Redwood | Updated weekly |
     | KMS/HSM | AWS KMS ARN or CloudHSM config | Customer Sec | Optional for Private |

3. Integration & Test (1-2 weeks)
   - Integration checklist (must pass):
     - API connectivity: successful cURL auth test and inference request.
     - Throughput smoke test: simulate 10-20% of expected QPS.
     - Latency baseline: measure p50/p95 under representative prompts.
     - Security audit: verify token rotation, RBAC, and audit logging.
     - Logging/tracing: ensure Trace ID header is captured end-to-end.

   - Example cURL smoke test:
     curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/infer \\n       -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED_API_KEY>' \\n       -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\n       -d '{"model":"redwood-1.5", "input":"Summarize the following: ..."}'

   - Example embedding test (Python):
     import requests
     resp = requests.post("https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings", json={"model":"embed-2","input":"example text"}, headers={"Authorization":"Bearer <KEY>"})
     print(resp.json())

   - Network validation commands (from customer):
     - TLS handshake: openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.ai:443 -servername api.redwood.ai
     - Firewall check: curl --connect-timeout 5 https://api.redwood.ai/health || echo 'connect failed'

4. Go-Live & Handover (1 week)
   - Staged rollout: start with 10% traffic for 48 hours, monitor errors and latency.
   - Canaries: set rollbacks triggered by: error_rate > 1.0% or p95_latency > target + 200ms for 30m window.
   - Handover checklist to Ops: runbooks, alerting thresholds, contacts, escalation paths.

2) Support Process and SLAs

Severity definitions and SLAs (support):
- P1 (Critical): Production outage or system-wide failure causing >25% request failures or total service unavailable. Response target: 1 hour. Target resolution or mitigation: 6 hours.
- P2 (High): Significant degradation (p95 latency > target + 500ms, or 5-25% request failures). Response target: 4 hours. Target resolution or mitigation: 24 hours.
- P3 (Medium): Feature degraded or non-critical functionality (rate limiting misconfig, SDK bug). Response target: 1 business day.
- P4 (Low): General questions, feature requests. Response target: 3 business days.

Support intake channels:
- Primary: Support ticketing portal (support.redwood.ai) — include org ID, Trace ID, timestamps, sample requests, and logs.
- Secondary: Email triage (enterprise-support@redwood.com) and CSM Slack channel for urgent coordination.

Ticket template (copy into ticket):
- Customer org ID: 
- Affected routes/models: 
- Severity (P1-P4): 
- Trace IDs / Request IDs (ISO timestamps): 
- Example payloads & response bodies: 
- Recent config changes (since last 24h): 
- Business impact and desired ETA: 

3) Escalation Playbook

When to escalate:
- If P1 unresolved after 1 hour, immediately page Escalation Engineer and notify CSM+SE.
- If external/supply chain (cloud provider) incident implicated, open joint incident bridge with Cloud Ops.

Escalation steps (numbered):
1. Triage in support ticket and reproduce the issue with customer-provided trace IDs.
2. Gather telemetry: p50/p95 latency, error rate, tokenization errors, GPU utilization, batch sizes, queue depth.
3. Map to potential causes: model runtime (hot loop), kernel OOM, network timeouts, customer traffic spike, misconfiguration.
4. If internal runtime suspected, page on-call runtime SRE and assign incident lead.
5. Coordinate mitigation: scale burst capacity, failover to safe model variant, increase autoscale targets, or apply temporary rate limiting.
6. Communicate status to customer every 30 minutes for P1 until mitigated.
7. Once resolved, run RCA and publish postmortem within 72 hours (P1) or 7 days (P2).

Communication templates (short):
- Initial ack (under 1 hour): "Thanks — we've received your ticket and are actively investigating. Current ETA for next update: 30 minutes. Team: <names>."
- Escalation notice: "We have escalated to Runtime SRE and Solutions Engineering. Mitigation steps in progress: <actions>. Next update in 30 minutes."
- Resolution: "Root cause identified: <summary>. Fix applied: <summary>. We will follow up with an RCA and suggested preventative steps."

4) Runbooks — Common incidents & playbooks

Incident: Increased p95 latency (sustained > target + 200ms for 30m)
- Owner: On-call runtime SRE
- Steps:
  1. Check service dashboard: per-route p50/p95, queue depth, GPU utilization.
  2. Query logs for "kv-cache-miss" or "batch-size" spikes.
  3. If queue depth > 80% capacity: increase worker pool or enable burst capacity.
  4. If model backend OOMs: reduce max_tokens or fallback to quantized model variant.
  5. If network errors are present: validate TCP retransmits and customer network path.
  6. Post-mitigation: collect perf traces and add to regression prompt set.

Incident: Auth failures for multiple customers
- Owner: Support + Auth Engineer
- Steps:
  1. Validate API keys in Redwood Console (revoked/rotated).
  2. Confirm client's clock skew < 5 minutes if using signed tokens.
  3. Check IAM and KMS connectivity for Private deployments.
  4. Provide temporary scoped key while root cause is resolved.

5) Known issues & workarounds (living table)

- Issue: Cold-start latency for larger models after inactivity
  Workaround: Keep a small warm pool (min_workers) or schedule periodic light probes (e.g., 1 inference / 5 minutes).

- Issue: Higher than expected token count due to client-side tokenization differences
  Workaround: Include tokenization tool in SDK (tokenizer.redwood.ai) and recommend server-side token counting.

- Issue: KV cache evictions during burst causing latency spikes
  Workaround: Increase kv_cache_size or configure sticky sessions for bursty clients; use model shard pinning for high-QPS routes.

- Issue: Model upload fails with "manifest missing" on Private deployments
  Workaround: Validate manifest.json matches spec (fields: model_id, architecture, weights_sha256, quantization_profile). Example manifest snippet:
  {
    "model_id": "customer/model-v1",
    "architecture": "decoder-only",
    "weights_sha256": "abc123...",
    "quantization_profile": "q4_0"
  }

6) Integration Guide — checklist & sample configs

Required headers
- Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>
- X-Redwood-Org: <ORG_ID>
- X-Request-Id / Trace-Id: <UUID> (set by caller if available)

Sample client config (YAML):
  redwood_client:
    api_url: https://api.redwood.ai
    api_key: "<SECRET>"
    timeout_s: 30
    max_retries: 3
    telemetry: true

Retry guidance:
- Use exponential backoff with jitter for 429/503. Do not retry on 4xx except 409 (idempotency).
- Max total retry time: 30s by default for user-facing requests. For background jobs, longer windows are acceptable.

7) Health checks and QBR materials

Recommended QBR cadence: initial 30/60/90-day reviews, then quarterly.

Key metrics to prepare for QBR (present as slides + appendix):
- Uptime (monthly): target 99.95% for Dedicated/Hosted; report for last 90d.
- Error rate by route: target < 0.5% (production).
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 baseline vs target (show trends).
- Cost metrics: cost per 1k tokens, cost per embedding, percentage savings from batching/caching.
- Usage: daily active users, requests per minute, top 10 prompt templates by volume.
- Model quality: top 10 prompt regressions (failed evals) and suggested rollbacks or fine-tune trials.
- Operational: number of incidents (P1/P2) in last quarter, mean time to acknowledge (MTTA), mean time to repair (MTTR).

QBR template outline:
1. Executive summary (1 slide): overall health, topline wins, open risks.
2. Metrics & trends (3-4 slides): latency, errors, cost, usage.
3. Recent incidents & RCA summary (1-2 slides).
4. Product roadmap & upcoming infra changes (1 slide).
5. Action items & commitments (1 slide): tickets, experiments, optimization plan.
6. Appendix: raw dashboards, configs, and regression prompt lists.

8) Postmortem and RCA guidance

- For P1 incidents produce a public-facing postmortem within 72 hours and a detailed internal RCA within one week. Include: timeline, root cause analysis, corrective actions, owners, and verification steps.
- Use the standard postmortem template: Summary, Impact, Root Cause, Corrective Actions, Preventative Actions, Timeline, Lessons Learned.

9) Templates & Artifacts (copyable)

Sample incident timeline entry (log):
- 2026-02-16T14:02:31Z — Error spike observed: route /v1/infer p95 increased to 950ms (baseline 400ms)
- 2026-02-16T14:07:10Z — On-call paged (runtime-sre)
- 2026-02-16T14:22:00Z — Mitigation: scaled worker pool + enabled fallback model
- 2026-02-16T15:30:00Z — Performance returned to baseline, monitoring continued

Support escalation Slack snippet (public channel):
"@here P1 incident for AcmeCorp: /v1/infer p95 > 2s. Paging runtime-sre and solutions-eng. Ticket #12345 created: <link>. Owning SE: Marco Ruiz."
